description:
Set an iPhone on a tripod beside the court and it becomes your serve speed board and line judge.

• Serve speed: every serve is detected and its speed estimated, in huge digits you can read from the bench
• Line calls: each bounce is called in, out or too close to call, with a spoken "Out!" and a broadcast-style replay
• Video: records at 1080p / 60 fps; replay any shot and export clips or the whole session

Another iPhone, or a browser on any phone, tablet or computer, follows live. No account, no cloud.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Put one iPhone in landscape on a tripod behind or beside the court and choose Camera
2. On a second iPhone choose Display and scan the code, or scan it with any browser
3. Start recording, play, then end the session and replay it from History
With only one phone, the camera records, analyzes and replays on its own.

SERVE SPEED
• Serves are recognized automatically at both ends
• Courtside speed board: the latest serve in full-screen digits, with max, average and trend

LINE CALLS
• In, out or "close to the line" after each bounce, for serves (the diagonal service box) and rallies
• Near half by default; singles or doubles lines
• A spoken "Out!" only when the ball is clearly out
• Replay any call: the flight, a zoom to the line and the mark

VIDEO AND HISTORY
• Every shot listed with speed, bounce and stroke; tap to watch it
• Grab a few seconds around any shot during a session; transfer the full recording afterwards
• Share a clip or save it to Photos (add-only; your library is never read)
• Not on court? Import a tennis video and get the same shot-by-shot analysis

BROWSER DISPLAY
Any other phone, tablet or computer can scan the QR code on the camera to see live data, the speed board and line calls in a browser. Nothing to install.

NO ACCOUNT, NO CLOUD
Recordings and results stay on your own devices. Pair over the same Wi-Fi, a Personal Hotspot or peer-to-peer Wi-Fi; links between app displays are TLS-encrypted. The browser display uses plain HTTP on your local network and is less protected than the app display, so use the app or the camera's Personal Hotspot when that matters.

PLEASE NOTE
• Speeds, bounces, line calls and stroke types are single-camera model estimates, not radar readings or official calls. When the evidence is missing, the value is shown as "—" with a reason, never counted as zero.
• The app's screens are in Chinese.
• The camera needs an iPhone 13 or later (including iPhone SE 3rd generation).
• No scoring.
promotionalText: Set an iPhone by the court: serve speed, line calls with a spoken "Out!" and every shot on video. Another phone or any browser follows live. No account needed.
whatsNew:
• Challenge and line-call replays stop on the last frame instead of redrawing
• After a spoken line call, other apps' music returns to its previous volume; the replay scale says "about N cm"
• Older browsers can open the browser display; a diagnostic package reads only the camera logs around that session
• Rows with no landing, no speed and a contact far off the court are no longer saved
• Replays no longer draw a flight from a contact point that could not have happened
• Serve detection can use a player's raised arm while poses are being read; if analysis falls behind, pose reading pauses and those serves are judged from the flight
• A serve can still receive a speed estimate when the ball is lost briefly after the net; with no credible flight the speed stays "—"
• A near-side ball followed only to around the bounce can still get a landing candidate; when that estimate is loose, the call stays "close to the line"
• A landing is no longer marked "close to the line" only because the fitted contact point ran away
• Speeds, landings and line calls are still single-camera estimates. This version changes the serve and landing rules, so the same recording can differ from 1.2
